sub: The four Gospels in one story · 6 BC – AD 30

stops.t: In the beginning was the Word
stops.d: before all time — and c. 6 BC
stops.before: Four hundred years after Malachi. Rome rules; Herod, an Idumean, is king by Rome's favour; the Temple he is rebuilding is the wonder of the East. The story begins three times.
stops.watch: John begins before Genesis: the Word who was God became flesh. Matthew begins with a family tree — count the women: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, Bathsheba — and Joseph's dream. Luke begins in the Temple with an old priest struck dumb, and an angel in Nazareth: 'Hail, full of grace' — and Mary's yes. Her song, the Magnificat, is Hannah's song reborn.
stops.after: A census, a journey south, and no room at the inn.

stops.before: Micah named the town seven centuries ago. Caesar's decree brings a carpenter and his pregnant wife to it.
stops.watch: The manger, the shepherds, the angels' Gloria; Simeon in the Temple, who has waited his whole life for this and now can die — 'a sign that shall be contradicted, and thy own soul a sword shall pierce'. Then Matthew: the magi and the star, Herod's fury, the flight into Egypt and the slaughter of the innocents. And the boy of twelve, lost for three days, found in his Father's house.
stops.after: Thirty silent years in Nazareth. Then a voice in the desert.

stops.before: John, Zechariah's son, is in the Jordan valley in camel hair, eating locusts, baptising crowds and calling the Pharisees a brood of vipers. The Elijah Malachi promised.
stops.watch: Jesus comes to be baptised — and heaven opens, the Spirit descends, a voice: 'This is my beloved Son.' Then forty days in the desert and three temptations, each answered from Deuteronomy. Luke's genealogy runs back not to Abraham but to Adam.
stops.after: John points, and two of his disciples follow the Lamb of God.

stops.before: John's Gospel tells the first year, before the others begin: a week of callings, and a wedding.
stops.watch: Andrew, Peter, Philip, Nathanael under the fig tree. Water into wine at Cana, the first sign, at his mother's word. The whip in the Temple. Nicodemus by night — 'unless a man be born again' and 'God so loved the world'. The Samaritan woman at Jacob's well, the longest conversation Jesus has with anyone in the Gospels.
stops.after: John is arrested. Jesus goes north to Galilee, and the kingdom is announced.

stops.t: The kingdom of God is at hand
stops.before: Nazareth rejects him — a prophet is not without honour except in his own country — and Capernaum, on the lake, becomes his town.
stops.watch: Mark's breathless first chapters: fishermen called from their nets, a demon shouting his name in the synagogue, Peter's mother-in-law, a leper, a paralytic lowered through the roof — 'thy sins are forgiven thee' — Levi the tax collector at his table, the twelve chosen on a mountain. Watch how quickly the scribes decide he must die.
stops.after: On a hillside above the lake, he sits down to teach.

stops.before: The new Moses goes up a mountain, but instead of receiving a law he gives one.
stops.watch: The Beatitudes; salt and light; 'you have heard it said… but I say to you'; love your enemies; the Our Father; the lilies of the field; the narrow gate; the house on rock. Three chapters that the world, believing or not, has never been able to put down.
stops.after: Words, then works — a day of miracles by the sea.

stops.before: The crowds are so thick he teaches from a boat. He speaks only in parables now — the sower, the seed growing secretly, the mustard seed.
stops.watch: The storm on the lake, and the question that hangs over the whole Gospel: 'Who is this, that both wind and sea obey him?' The Gerasene demoniac and the pigs; Jairus's daughter and the woman who touched his cloak; the Baptist's head on a dish; five loaves and two fish for five thousand; and Jesus walking on the water.
stops.after: After the bread, a hard saying, and many walk away.

stops.t: I am the bread of life
stops.before: The crowd he fed wants to make him king. In the synagogue at Capernaum he tells them what the bread means.
stops.watch: 'Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood…' — and 'Will you also go away?' Peter: 'Lord, to whom shall we go?' Mark 7–8: what defiles a man, the Syrophoenician woman's crumbs, the deaf man, and at Caesarea Philippi the confession — 'Thou art the Christ' — followed at once by the first prediction of the cross, and Peter rebuked.
stops.after: Six days later, on a high mountain, three of them see him as he is.

stops.before: Peter, James and John go up the mountain with him and he begins to pray.
stops.watch: His face shining like the sun, Moses and Elijah — the Law and the Prophets — talking with him about his 'departure' at Jerusalem, the cloud, the voice. Then straight down into a crowd and a boy no one could heal: 'I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.' Matthew 18: the child in the midst, the lost sheep, seventy times seven.
stops.after: He sets his face toward Jerusalem, and Luke gives him a long road to teach on.

stops.before: Luke's 'travel narrative' — ten chapters on the way south, full of the parables only he records.
stops.watch: The seventy-two sent out; the Good Samaritan; Martha and Mary; the rich fool; the narrow door; the great supper; the lost sheep, the lost coin and the lost son — the Prodigal, the finest short story ever told; the dishonest steward; Lazarus and the rich man; the Pharisee and the publican.
stops.after: In Jerusalem for the feasts, John shows the quarrel sharpening.

stops.before: At Tabernacles and at the Dedication, in Herod's Temple, Jesus speaks in the open and the authorities try to arrest him.
stops.watch: The woman taken in adultery and the finger writing in the dust; 'I am the light of the world'; the man born blind, whose parents are afraid and who ends up seeing more than the Pharisees; the good shepherd who lays down his life; and the claim that makes them pick up stones: 'Before Abraham was made, I AM.'
stops.after: A message comes from Bethany: the one you love is sick.

stops.before: Jesus waits two days, then goes to a tomb four days sealed. Martha meets him on the road: 'If thou hadst been here…'
stops.watch: 'I am the resurrection and the life.' Jesus wept. The stone, the cry, the man bound in grave-clothes. From that day the council decides he must die — 'it is expedient that one man should die for the people'. Mary anoints his feet; Zacchaeus climbs his tree in Jericho; and on Sunday, the colt and the palms.
stops.after: Holy Week. Every hour of it is written down.

stops.t: The Temple, the fig tree, the widow's coins
stops.before: Jesus enters the city as the prophets said the king would, on a donkey, and goes straight to the Temple. Read with the diagram of Herod's Temple open.
stops.watch: The tables overturned in the Court of the Gentiles; the fig tree; the wicked tenants — told to the priests' faces; the coin with Caesar's head; the widow's two mites in the treasury; and, on the Mount of Olives, the prophecy that not one stone will be left, the abomination of desolation, the Son of man coming on the clouds. Matthew adds the ten virgins, the talents, the sheep and the goats.
stops.after: Thursday evening. An upper room, a basin, a loaf and a cup.

stops.before: Judas has already gone to the priests. Jesus sends two disciples after a man carrying a water jar to find the room.
stops.watch: 'This is my body… this is the chalice of my blood' — the Passover become the Eucharist. In John, no bread and wine but the washing of feet, the new commandment, 'I am the way', the vine and the branches, the promise of the Paraclete, and the long prayer of chapter 17: 'that they may be one.' Then out, across the Kidron, to a garden.
stops.after: Gethsemane, the kiss, the trial, the cock-crow, the cross.

stops.before: Follow the map: the garden, the high priest's house, the praetorium, Golgotha — a few hundred paces each, between nine at night and three in the afternoon.
stops.watch: 'Not what I will, but what thou wilt.' Peter's three denials; 'Are you the king of the Jews?'; Barabbas; the scourging and the crown; Ecce homo; Simon of Cyrene; the seven last words across the four Gospels — 'Father, forgive them', 'this day thou shalt be with me in paradise', 'Woman, behold thy son', 'why hast thou forsaken me', 'I thirst', 'It is consummated', 'into thy hands'. The veil torn; the centurion; Joseph's new tomb.
stops.after: The Sabbath. Then, before dawn on the first day of the week, women with spices.

stops.before: The stone is rolled away and the tomb is empty. Each Gospel tells the morning differently, and all four agree on that.
stops.watch: Mary Magdalene and the gardener — 'Mary.' Peter and John running; the road to Emmaus and the breaking of bread; Thomas's hand in the wound; breakfast on the beach and 'Simon, son of John, lovest thou me?' three times, for three denials; 'Go, teach all nations… I am with you all days.' And the Ascension from the Mount of Olives.
stops.after: Ten days later, a sound like a mighty wind.
